title: De Peccatorum Meritis et Remissione et de Baptismo Parvulorum
author: Augustine

passages.original: Vnde non inmerito beatus Cyprianus satis ostendit, quam hoc ab initio creditum et intellectum seruet ecclesia. qui cum paruulos a materno utero recentissimos iam idoneos ad percipiendum Christi baptismum adsereret, quoniam consultus fuerat, utrum hoc ante octauum diem fieri deberet, quantum potuit, conatus est eos demonstrare perfectos, ne quis ipso numero dierum, quo octauo antea circumcidebantur infantes, eos adhuc perficiendos existimaret.
passages.english: Hence not without reason the blessed Cyprian shows clearly enough how [firmly] the church preserves this [doctrine] as believed and understood from the beginning. For when he was asserting that little ones, newly come from their mother's womb, are already fit to receive the baptism of Christ, since he had been consulted whether this ought to be done before the eighth day, he tried, as far as he could, to show that they are complete, lest anyone should think, on account of the very number of days (since infants were formerly circumcised on the eighth), that they were still to be made complete.
passages.notes: "quam hoc ... seruet": "quam" is taken as intensifying ("how firmly"); the adverb is supplied in brackets. "perfectos"/"perficiendos" refers to the infants being complete, fully formed, and so fit for baptism, as against needing to wait until the eighth day.
